profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
The P. Gannavaram Assembly Constituency Vision Action Plan 2024-29 has been meticulously designed to leverage the constituency's agricultural strength, dynamic industrial base, thriving construction sector, and robust service sector. This strategic blueprint aligns with Andhra Pradesh’s ambitious Swarna Andhra@2047 vision, which resonates with the national agenda of Viksit Bharat@2047 P. Gannavaram Constituency consists of four mandals1. Ainavilli

2. Ambajipeta3.P. Gannavaram. Part of Mamidikuduru Mandal (11 village) These are located in the Dr.B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema District of Andhra Pradesh. P. Gannavaram serving as the Head-Quarters. It is one of the seven assembly segments of the Amalapuram Lok-Sabha constituency. There is a total of 189,258 electors in the constituency. The constituency established in 2008 per the Delimitation orders (2008). P. Gannavaram has a rich history dating back to ancient times. The village is believed to have been formed when Sage Vainateya stole part of the Vashishta River from Sage Vashishta, who cursed him for his actions. To lift the curse, Vainateya prayed to Garuda, the vehicle of lord Vishnu, to bring a Sivalingam from Varanasi. While bringing the Sivalingam, Garuda’s hand slipped, and it fell down in this village, which was then installed and became known as Garudavaram, later known as Gannavaram

economy_text.economy_Text:
P Gannavaram’s Economy at a Glance


The Economic Vision Plan for P. Gannavaram lays a structured path for accelerating economic growth, boosting employment, and ensuring inclusive development. With a Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) of ₹3,893 crores in 2023-24, P. Gannavaram is projected to expand steadily, reaching ₹8611 crores by 2028-29, marking a significant transformation across agriculture, industry, and services sectors. The industrial sector accounts for 13.86%, agriculture and allied activities contribute 49.84% and service sector contributes 36.30%.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: P Gannavaram is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like horticulture, Fishing & Aquaculture and construction. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant urban and economic hub by 2047.
